name: The Vanderbilt, Auberge Collection
positioning: Historic mansion hotel in downtown Newport, Rhode Island, part of Auberge Collection, with interiors by the design studio SWOON
best_for: Travelers who want a historic mansion hotel in downtown Newport
Families and groups wanting connecting suites

facts.text: The property was originally built in 1908 by Alfred Gwynne Vanderbilt.
The interiors were reimagined by the design collective SWOON.
The hotel features a commissioned series by photographer and artist Maxine Helfman.
The Library is a parlor near the lobby with a hidden honor bar.
The Conservatory serves breakfast, lunch and afternoon tea.
The Roof Deck is a rooftop bar with views of Newport Harbor.
The Dining Room at The Vanderbilt serves a menu of approachable New England classics.
The hotel has a spa and fitness center with indoor and outdoor pools.
A number of suites can be connected to each other, which suits families and groups.
The hotel is at 41 Mary St. in Newport, Rhode Island.

highlights.text: Beneath the scenic wallpaper in the Library, a secret door leads to a coral-coated liquor cabinet.
Guests can take a hands-on tour of furniture maker Jonathan Glatt's showroom in Warren, Rhode Island.
Guests can take a private tour of Matunuck Oyster Farm to learn how oysters are cultivated.
Guests can visit a neighboring shipbuilder's workshop to see antique boat restoration.

considerations.text: Entry-level rooms are on the cozy side.
Guest rooms could be improved with more direct water views.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the exclusive Newport location.
